title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions that define the student experience at Bates College, from icy plunges to historic masonry.

cards.title: The Puddle Jump
cards.subtitle: A Mid-Winter Polar Plunge
cards.notes: Join hundreds of students in late winter to jump through a hole cut in the ice of Lake Andrews, a tradition started in 1975 to celebrate the end of a hard Maine winter.
cards.short_summary: An annual winter tradition where students jump into the icy waters of Lake Andrews.
cards.evidence_claim: The Puddle Jump began in 1975 when students cut a hole in the ice on Lake Andrews for a St. Patrick's Day dip; it now features a 'Dip Master' and an official ax.
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually during Winter Carnival; open to all students to watch or participate.

cards.title: Ivy Stones
cards.subtitle: Class Year Masonry
cards.notes: Look for engraved granite plaques set into the brickwork of campus buildings; each graduating class since 1879 has designed and installed a unique stone to mark their legacy.
cards.short_summary: A tradition of installing custom-designed class year plaques into campus buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Since the 1870s, engraved plaques known as ivy stones have been installed in Bates campus buildings to honor each graduating class, with the first placed in 1878.
cards.source_title: Bates ivy stones from 1879 to today | Campus Tour
cards.access_notes: Stones are visible year-round on the exterior of various campus buildings.

cards.title: Winter Carnival Torch Relay
cards.subtitle: Governor-Lit Tradition
cards.notes: Watch the arrival of the carnival torch, traditionally lit by the Governor of Maine and relayed by students from the state capital in Augusta to the Lewiston campus.
cards.short_summary: A torch relay from Augusta to campus that kicks off the annual Winter Carnival.
cards.evidence_claim: The torch relay tradition began in 1958 when Governor Edmund Muskie lit a torch that students relayed from Augusta to campus for the Winter Carnival opening parade.
cards.source_title: January 1958: The Winter Carnival torch tradition | 150 Years | Bates College
cards.access_notes: The relay occurs annually in late January or early February during Winter Carnival.

cards.title: Harvest Dinner
cards.subtitle: A Campus-Wide Feast
cards.notes: Experience the annual themed Thanksgiving-style feast at Commons, featuring elaborate ice sculptures and a menu of regional favorites like Italian pudding.
cards.short_summary: An elaborate annual themed dinner hosted by Dining Services for the entire community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harvest Dinner is a 40-year-old tradition hosted by Commons around November 19th, featuring ice sculptures and a themed buffet.
cards.source_title: Let's Get Traditional: The Best Bates Traditions - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Held annually in November; requires a meal plan or guest pass for entry.

cards.title: Commencement Sunrise Climb
cards.subtitle: Senior Class Farewell
cards.notes: Climb the rocky summit of Mount David on the morning of Commencement to watch the sunrise with fellow graduates, a final reflective moment before the ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A tradition where graduating seniors climb Mount David to watch the sunrise together.
cards.evidence_claim: Graduating seniors climb Mount David on the night before Commencement to watch the morning sunrise together as a class tradition.
cards.source_title: Mount David | Campus Tour - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible via trails off Mountain Avenue; the sunrise climb is specific to Commencement morning.

cards.title: Village Club Series (VCS)
cards.subtitle: Thursday Night Coffeehouse
cards.notes: Attend this student-run performance series every Thursday night for live music and a coffeehouse atmosphere in the Benjamin Mays Center.
cards.short_summary: A long-running weekly performance series featuring student and guest artists.
cards.evidence_claim: The Village Club Series (VCS) has been a Bates institution since 1993, held most Thursdays at 8:00pm in the Benjamin Mays Center.
cards.source_title: Village Club Series | Campus Life - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Events typically start at 8:00 PM on Thursdays during the academic year.

cards.title: Lick-It Dance
cards.subtitle: Queer-Centric Celebration
cards.notes: Participate in this high-energy, costume-heavy dance hosted by OutFront, traditionally held in the Gray Cage as a celebration of queer identity and expression.
cards.short_summary: An annual inclusive dance event focused on queer community and creative costumes.
cards.evidence_claim: Lick-It is an annual dance event hosted by the student group OutFront, known for its expressive costumes and focus on queer identity.
cards.source_title: Important Information for Attendees of Lick-It 2026 | Campus Life | Bates College
cards.access_notes: Held annually in March; open to Bates students and registered guests.

cards.title: The Napkin Board
cards.subtitle: Dining Hall Feedback Loop
cards.notes: Read the physical or digital board in Commons where students post questions on napkins and receive direct, often humorous, responses from Dining Services staff.
cards.short_summary: A unique communication tradition between students and dining staff via napkins.
cards.evidence_claim: The Napkin Board in Commons allows students to communicate with Dining Services; it has both a physical presence and an online version.
cards.source_title: Online Napkin Board | Dining, Conferences and Campus Events (DCCE) - Bates College
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Commons operating hours; digital version available online.

cards.title: The 80s Dance
cards.subtitle: Neon Nostalgia
cards.notes: Don your best neon spandex and vintage gear for the first major social event of the year, featuring 1980s hits and a massive outdoor dance floor on the Library Quad.
cards.short_summary: A massive outdoor dance party themed to the 1980s held early in the fall semester.
cards.evidence_claim: The 80s Dance is described as the first big social event of the year at Bates, typically held on the Library Quad with pizza and 80s music.
cards.source_title: Definitive Ranking of Bates Dances So Far - Her Campus
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the fall; open to the Bates student community.

cards.title: Dinger Day
cards.subtitle: Short Term Softball
cards.notes: Compete in or watch the campus-wide softball tournament held during the final week of Short Term, a high-energy athletic tradition that marks the end of the academic year.
cards.short_summary: A competitive campus-wide softball tournament held during the spring Short Term.
cards.evidence_claim: Dinger Day is a relatively new tradition involving a campus-wide softball tournament held on the last Saturday of Short Term.
cards.source_title: Let's Get Traditional: The Best Bates Traditions - The Bates Student
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually in late May during the final week of Short Term.
